source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: Having heard that most wonderful statement from Agastya, Rama, out of both respect and wonder, began to ask again.
verses.2: O venerable one, how could that dreadful forest, where King Shveta of Vidarbha performed penance, be devoid of deer and birds?
verses.3: I truly wish to hear how that king entered such a desolate forest, devoid of humans, to perform penance.
verses.4: Having heard Rama's words, which were filled with curiosity, the highly effulgent Agastya indeed began to speak.
verses.5: O Rama, formerly in the Krita Yuga, there was a powerful lord named Manu, the wielder of the scepter, and his great son, Ikshvaku, was the delight of his family.
verses.6: Having placed that unconquerable first-born son in the kingdom on earth, Manu said to him, "Become the founder of royal dynasties on this earth."
verses.7: O Rama, the son assented to his father's command, and then Manu, extremely pleased, spoke to his son.
verses.8: Manu said, "O most generous one, I am pleased; you are indeed the creator, of this there is no doubt; protect the subjects with justice, but do not inflict punishment without cause."
verses.9: The punishment that is properly inflicted upon offenders among men, when administered according to law, leads the king to heaven.
verses.10: Therefore, O mighty-armed son, be diligent in administering justice, for by doing so, supreme righteousness will be yours in this world.
verses.11: Having thus given many instructions to his son with a composed mind, Manu, delighted, went to the eternal world of Brahma, which is heaven.
verses.12: When Manu had departed to heaven, Ikshvaku, who was of immeasurable splendor, became absorbed in the thought, "How shall I beget sons?"
verses.13: The righteous son of Manu, Ikshvaku, then begot a hundred sons, resembling the sons of gods, through various kinds of rituals and deeds.
verses.14: O dear Rama, the delight of the Raghu dynasty, the youngest among all those sons was foolish and uneducated, and he did not serve his elders.
verses.15: His father named that dull-witted son Danda, thinking that punishment would certainly befall his body.
verses.16: O Raghava, O destroyer of enemies, not finding that dreadful region of Lavana suitable, he (Shatrughna) established a kingdom in the middle of the Vindhya and Shaivala mountains.
verses.17: O Rama, he (Shatrughna), the wielder of justice, became king there on the beautiful mountain slope and established an unequalled, unsurpassed city.
verses.18: And, O Lord, he named the city Madhumanta and indeed chose the righteous Ushanas as his priest.
verses.19: Thus, that king (Shatrughna), with his priest, ruled that kingdom, which was filled with joyful people, just as Indra rules the kingdom of the gods.
verses.20: Then, that great-souled king, the son of the lord of men (Shatrughna), together with Ushanas at that time, ruled the very great kingdom, just as Indra, accompanied by Ushanas, rules in heaven. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनशीतितमः सर्गः ।। 79 ।। Thus ends the seventy-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
